user.title: Add Truma iNet X
user.description: Select the Truma panel to add.

data_description.address: The Truma panel to pair with. Only panels currently advertising within range of Home Assistant's Bluetooth, whether that is an ESP32 proxy or a local adapter, are listed.

confirm.description: Do you want to add the Truma panel {name}?

pair.title: Pair with the Truma panel
pair.description:
Put the panel {name} into add-device mode (in the Truma InetX app, or on the panel itself), then select **Submit** once. Pairing can take up to a minute.

**If pairing fails, work through these in order:**

1. **Clear the panel's saved Bluetooth device list.** It stores only about four devices and silently rejects new bonds once full. Put the panel back into add-device mode and try again.
2. **If clearing the list did not help, power-cycle the panel and start over** — switch it off, back on, put it into add-device mode again, and repeat this step. A power-cycle drops stale connections that hold a slot and makes the panel advertise a fresh Bluetooth address, which pairs cleanly. This resolves most stubborn cases.

Always re-enter add-device mode before each attempt: the panel only accepts a bond while its pairing screen is up.

data.forget_bond: Forget this host's existing bond and retry

data_description.forget_bond: Tick this only if arming the panel did not help. A panel that is not in add-device mode refuses a pairing attempt in exactly the same way as a panel that has forgotten this Home Assistant, so removing an existing bond on that evidence can destroy a working one. Ticking this discards the bond on this host and pairs from scratch.

unnamed.title: Truma panel seen, but it has no name
unnamed.description:
A Truma panel is advertising at **{address}**, so it is in range and being heard — but its name is not arriving, and the name is what a Truma entry is keyed on.

The name travels in a *scan response*, and only an **active** scan asks for one. A scanner that is passively listening therefore never receives it. Nothing is wrong with the panel.

Scanners here:

> {scanners}

**To fix it:** enable active scanning on that adapter, or — if it is an ESP32 proxy — set `bluetooth_proxy: active: true` (the official Bluetooth Proxy firmware already does). The panel then appears again, with its name, ready to add.

error.pairing_failed: Could not pair with the panel. Put it back into add-device mode and try again. If that fails, clear its saved Bluetooth device list (it holds only about four devices); if clearing the list does not help either, power-cycle the panel, put it into add-device mode again and start over.
error.pairing_failed_no_bond: Could not pair, and this Home Assistant held **no bond** to the panel before the attempt — so the panel is either still storing an entry for a host that no longer has its key, or it is not accepting new bonds. On the panel: remove this Home Assistant from its Bluetooth device list, clear that list (it holds only about four devices), then put the panel into add-device mode and try again. If that fails too, power-cycle the panel and repeat.
error.bond_still_working:
This Home Assistant already has a working bond to the panel — it is talking to it right now, so nothing was attempted and nothing was changed.

A re-pair is only needed when the panel has forgotten this host. On the panel: remove this Home Assistant, clear its saved device list, then put the panel into add-device mode. Then tick **forget the stale bond** below and continue.

abort.no_devices_found: No Truma iNet X panels found. Make sure the panel is powered on and in Bluetooth range.
abort.already_configured: This Truma panel is already configured.
abort.awaiting_name: Waiting for the Truma panel to advertise its name before pairing.
abort.reconfigure_successful: Re-paired with the Truma panel successfully.

control_not_ready.message: Truma BLE control is not available yet (transport is wired in a later build stage).

no_route.title: Nothing can connect to the Truma panel
no_route.description:
Home Assistant can hear the Truma panel advertising, but no adapter or proxy it has can connect to it. Two different faults look like this, and the first one is inside Home Assistant and fixed in a click.

**1. Home Assistant's Bluetooth integration has lost its own view of the panel.** Its advertisement store can hold the panel under one address while the per-address lookup a connect uses is keyed on another, so it reports that nothing can reach a panel it heard seconds ago. Measured on this panel on 2026-10-25: reloading the Bluetooth integration made the session come up straight away, with nothing changed on the host or the panel. Try that first — **Settings → Devices & Services → Bluetooth**, then the **⋮** menu → **Reload**. It costs a few seconds and touches no pairing.

**2. Or this host cannot put the panel's current address on air.** The panel uses a rotating private address and only answers a connect that carries its *current* one. Whether a given host manages that is a property of its controller and kernel: some do it in software, some send the panel's identity address instead (which the panel does not answer), and an ESPHome Bluetooth proxy's controller does it itself. Which side your host is on cannot be read from here, only tested — one installation with a current kernel carries the session locally at 18 of 18 devices — so change nothing else until the reload above has been tried.

If the reload did not help, check that the panel is in range of whichever adapter or proxy you have, and that nothing else is holding a connection to it. A bond lives on the adapter it was made with: if the adapter or proxy that paired the panel is gone, the panel has to be paired again.

Home Assistant chooses which adapter or proxy to connect through by itself; this integration does not pin the panel to one.

panel_silent.title: The Truma panel stopped answering
panel_silent.description:
Home Assistant connected to the Truma panel and the link came up, but every device on its internal bus stayed silent. The panel's radio is working; the panel is not.

This is not a Bluetooth problem on your side, and reconnecting does not help — on this hardware each attempt leaves it worse, which is why the integration has stopped trying for a while.

**Power-cycle the panel**: switch it off and on again, or pull its fuse for a few seconds. The integration retries every 30 minutes, and this message disappears by itself once the panel answers again.

panel_refusing.title: The Truma panel refuses to connect
panel_refusing.description:
The panel is advertising and Home Assistant holds a bond for it, but every connection is refused.

The usual cause is that the panel no longer recognises this Home Assistant. It forgets a paired device if its Bluetooth stack crashes (the panel itself may show something like "bluetooth not available" on its screen), or when its device list is cleared.

To fix it:

1. On the panel, remove this Home Assistant from its device list — or clear the list if that is easier.
2. Open the integration, choose **Configure → Reconfigure**, and tick **forget the stale bond**.
3. Put the panel into add-device (pairing) mode when asked, and submit once.

If the panel still refuses afterwards, its Bluetooth has not recovered: power-cycle the panel (off for ten seconds, then on) and try again.

panel_unnamed.title: Truma panel heard, but it cannot be named
panel_unnamed.description:
A Truma panel is advertising at **{address}** and Home Assistant is hearing it, but its name is not arriving — and the name is what a Truma entry is keyed on, so no discovery card can offer it for setup.

The name travels in a *scan response*, and only an **active** scan asks for one. A scanner that is passively listening therefore never receives it. Nothing is wrong with the panel.

Scanners here:

> {scanners}

**To fix it:** enable active scanning on that adapter, or — if it is an ESP32 proxy — set `bluetooth_proxy: active: true` (the official Bluetooth Proxy firmware already does). This entry disappears by itself once the panel's name is heard.

scanner_passive.title: The Bluetooth adapter never asks the Truma panel for its name
scanner_passive.description:
Home Assistant can hear the Truma panel, but nothing it sends carries a name — and the name is what this entry is keyed on. A name only travels in a *scan response*, and this host is configured to scan **passively**, so it will never ask for one: {scanners}.

Nothing is wrong with the panel, and reloading or restarting anything will not change this — the request is never made in the first place.

**1. Turn active scanning on.** Settings → Devices & Services → Bluetooth → **⋮** → *Configure* → scanning mode **Active**. For an ESPHome Bluetooth Proxy, set `bluetooth_proxy: active: true` in its YAML instead (the official proxy firmware already scans actively).

**2. Or connect through a proxy that scans actively**, which asks for the scan response on the panel's behalf.

This message clears itself once a scan response arrives. Background: a controller that refuses `LE Set Scan Parameters` (HCI opcode 0x2013) makes the Bluetooth stack silently fall back to passive scanning — the panel is then audible but nameless, and the fault is in the host's radio, not in the panel.

host_deaf.title: Home Assistant has stopped hearing Bluetooth
host_deaf.description:
No Bluetooth device has been heard on this host for about {minutes} minutes — not the Truma panel, not anything else. That is what makes this a fault in the machine running Home Assistant rather than in the panel: a panel that is switched off, asleep or out of range goes quiet on its own, but everything else keeps arriving.

**1. Reload the Bluetooth integration.** Settings → Devices & Services → Bluetooth → **⋮** → *Reload*. It costs a few seconds and touches no pairing.

**2. If the adapter is a USB dongle, unplug it and plug it back in** — a controller that has stopped answering is usually reset by its own power cycle.

**If neither helps, this is outside this integration.** It registers a listener for advertisements and asks Home Assistant to connect; it never starts or stops scanning, never resets an adapter and never restarts Bluetooth. A radio that has stopped answering after a controller refusal (the kernel records `Opcode 0x2013 failed`, which the host log keeps) needs the host itself — that is where to look, and this card will clear by itself once anything is heard again.

data_description.poll_interval_seconds: 0 keeps the connection open, so changes show up instantly. A non-zero value connects, takes a reading and disconnects again -- slower, but it frees the adapter's connection slot between readings, which matters when other Bluetooth devices share the same adapter.
